institution: National Centre for Disease Control, National AMR Surveillance Network (NARS-Net)
citation: National Centre for Disease Control. Annual Report 2021: National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network (NARS-Net India), reporting period 1 January to 31 December 2020. New Delhi: National Programme on AMR Containment, NCDC, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; 2021.
reporting: Number tested, number resistant and percent resistant (%R) by specimen type (blood; pus aspirate with other sterile body fluids together, PA+OSBF; urine), all location types combined; all specimens together in Table 5 (S. aureus) and in charts printing number resistant, percentage and number tested (Enterococcus, E. coli, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter); location-type charts (IN, OUT, ICU) with printed data labels and isolate numbers in the legends; trend charts 2017 to 2020 (MRSA, linezolid resistance in S. aureus and Enterococcus, imipenem and minocycline resistance in Acinetobacter).
method: WHONET; first identification and AST result per patient and specimen type (57,282 isolates reported, 55,688 unique patient isolates analysed); disk diffusion, broth microdilution or automated AST; colistin by broth microdilution per CLSI M02 and M100 for a limited number of isolates; breakpoint edition not stated; no vancomycin broth microdilution results for S. aureus.

verification.note: Tables 5, 7 to 12 parsed from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF words assigned to the number tested, number resistant and %R columns of each specimen group by their left edges; multi-line drug names joined) and every value then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 to 2.6 (tables cropped). Every printed %R was recomputed from its printed counts: all agree within rounding except S. aureus blood doxycycline (conflict); Table 10 gives no number resistant for S. Typhi, so each of its percentages was only checked to be possible for its number tested. Table 2 counts transcribed from the text layer, compared with the page and checked against the column totals (13,793, 23,122, 19,044 and 1). Overall charts (Figures 12, 16, 18, 21, 23): the "number resistant; %" and "number tested" labels matched to their bars from the PDF drawing and to the drug by position, each percentage recomputed from its two counts, each bar length checked against its label, and each percentage compared with the specimen table columns added together (all within 0.6 points). Location charts (Figures 10, 13, 14, 17, 19, 22, 24) and Figures 20a and 20b: each data label matched to its bar (label beside the bar end, bar colour to the legend marker; bars run IN, OUT, ICU from the top), bar lengths within 0.6 of their labels, bars not drawn (0) placed by their position; every chart then checked by eye on the rendered page. Trend labels of Figures 9, 15 and 25 from the text layer and Figure 11 (an image) read from the page zoomed. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (1-based).

notes: Fourth NARS-Net annual report (titled Annual Report-2021; the PDF file is dated 17 January 2022): 29 medical college laboratories in 24 states and UTs reporting, seven priority bacterial pathogens, January to December 2020, a year in which many laboratories were diverted to COVID-19 testing (the report advises caution in comparing 2020 with earlier years). All figures are percent resistant as printed (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimens: pus aspirate and other sterile body fluids are given together (PA + OSBF), shown here under deep infections; the S. aureus Table 5 "Blood + PA + OSBF" column is shown as all specimens except urine (S. aureus is not collected from urine, so for it this is every specimen under surveillance), and all-specimen rows come from the overall charts (Figures 12, 16, 18, 21, 23), which count isolates per patient and so slightly fewer than the specimen tables. NARS-Net does not collect respiratory specimens. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows (ward = IN, outpatients = OUT, ICU) come from bar charts with printed data labels and isolate numbers in the legends; the Enterococcus chart for blood with PA and OSBF is recorded as all specimens except urine. Trends 2017 to 2020 (Figures 9, 11, 15, 25) are attached to the all-specimen rows. Table 2 prints the Acinetobacter urine count as "9,73"; its column total (23,122), Figure 5, Table 12 (N=973) and the text (page 41) give 973. Only S. Typhi has percentages for Salmonella. Grey table cells are absent. No fungal data in this edition.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 89 of 356 cells (every table and chart), every row n and every count were read from the page images (scale 3, tables and charts cropped) and written down before comparing; every other cell was then read as well: all 356 cells, all 208 numbers tested, all 45 row n, all 19 counts (Table 2, page 19) and the five trend series (Figures 9, 11, 15 and 25). 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. The validator's caution list prints the value of its one caution cell (S. aureus blood doxycycline), which is in the sample, so that cell was not read blind; it was confirmed on the page.

Location charts (Figures 10, 13, 14, 17, 19, 22, 24): each label checked against its bar (light blue IN, green OUT, dark blue ICU from the top, bar end at the label's value), organism and specimen from the chart title. The legend N of the all-specimen charts equal the ICU, IPD and OPD columns of Table 4 (Pseudomonas IN 3,973 against 3,974, already noted), so IN is non-ICU inpatients (ward). Overall charts (Figures 12, 16, 18, 21, 23): each "number resistant; %" label and number tested matched to its drug, and each percentage fits its two counts. No setting, specimen or organism swaps.

Caution confirmed as printed: Table 5 S. aureus blood doxycycline prints 2,638 tested, 24 resistant, 12% (a source error; the all-specimen 725 of 5,489 less PA + OSBF 402 leaves 323, 12.2%), kept with its conflict. Klebsiella urine nitrofurantoin 41 confirmed as printed in Figure 20a: the label sits on the Klebsiella bar (green, legend Klebsiella spp. N=4,717, bar length 41; the E. coli bar is 12). Table 2 prints the Acinetobacter urine count as "9,73"; 973 is confirmed by the urine column total (23,122 less the other four organisms leaves 973), Figure 5 (page 20), Table 12 (Urine N=973) and the text (page 41).

Every printed %R of Tables 5, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 recomputed from its printed counts: all within rounding (several at x.46 to x.50 printed up, for example S. aureus PA + OSBF cefoxitin 2,357 of 4,580 = 51.46, printed 52), except the doxycycline conflict and Klebsiella blood colistin (12 of 814 = 1.5%, printed 2%), which its per-drug note already records. The five 1 point differences between Figure 20b and Table 8 (E. coli blood) confirmed as noted on the row.
